title: Harden browser ESM build: stub Node builtins instead of emitting bare import "fs"/"path"
description: PR #1263's browser-targeted ESM (dist/esm/index.mjs) still emits bare Node-builtin imports (import "fs" in concerto-core and concerto-util, import "path" in concerto-util) because scripts/build-esm.js externalizes builtinModules for all builds. This only resolves in downstream consumers that ship Node-polyfill/fallback infrastructure (concerto-playground via vite-plugin-node-polyfills, template-engine via webpack resolve.fallback). A stricter consumer (plain esbuild/rollup/Vite without polyfills) would fail with unresolved 'fs'/'path'. The existing webpack UMD build already avoids this by mapping fs/tls/net/child_process/os/path -> false (empty stub). Fix: for browser builds only, stub Node builtins to empty modules via an esbuild plugin instead of externalizing them, achieving parity with the UMD. Keep externalizing builtins for the node-only linter build.

title: Spike E: per-export native-ESM migration measurement (leaf module) — GO/NO-GO
description: Throwaway worktree. Migrate one low-fan-in concerto-core leaf module export=/import=require -> native ESM. Measure single-export vs whole-index bundle bytes. Write GO/NO-GO memo. DISCARD worktree; nothing merges. Model: sonnet.
notes:
## Spike E — GO/NO-GO Memo: Native ESM Migration for Per-Export Tree-Shaking

### Setup
- Worktree: /tmp/wt-spike at commit 3073809b8 (rebased branch)
- Leaf module tested: packages/concerto-core/src/securityexception.ts
- Reason chosen: zero internal ./ requires, only one external dep (BaseException from @accordproject/concerto-util)
- Measurement tool: esbuild --bundle --minify --platform=node

---

### BEFORE Baseline (current: esbuild bundle:true, CJS-in-ESM blob)

| Import | Bundle size |
|--------|------------|
| 1 export (SecurityException only) | 595,862 bytes (596 KB) |
| All exports (export * from index) | 596,715 bytes (597 KB) |
| Delta (1 export vs all) | 853 bytes (0.14%) |

**Interpretation:** Virtually no per-export tree-shaking. Importing one class vs the entire library differs by less than 1 KB because the whole concerto-core source (all 58 TS files + third-party deps) is pre-bundled into a single CJS-in-ESM blob using __commonJS/__esm wrappers. Bundlers cannot tree-shake inside this blob.

---

### AFTER Measurement (migrated securityexception.ts to native ESM, bundle:false)

Migration performed: Changed securityexception.ts from:
  const { BaseException } = require('@accordproject/concerto-util');  ... export = SecurityException;
To:
  import { BaseException } from '@accordproject/concerto-util';  ... export { SecurityException };

Compiled with esbuild bundle:false → 385-byte unbundled .mjs file with live import statement.

Consumer bundler then tree-shakes the import chain (SecurityException → BaseException only).

| Import | Bundle size |
|--------|------------|
| 1 export (SecurityException from unbundled .mjs) | 22,908 bytes (22 KB) |
| Reduction vs BEFORE | **96.2%** (573 KB saved) |

The 22 KB is: SecurityException itself + the portion of @accordproject/concerto-util's bundled blob needed for BaseException. Note: concerto-util is ALSO a bundled CJS-in-ESM blob — if concerto-util were also migrated to native ESM, the after-bundle would be even smaller (BaseException is ~30 lines; full tree-shaken size would be <1 KB).

---

### Migration Cost Assessment

**Files requiring migration:** 58 total with export = / CJS require patterns.

**Pure leaf files (no internal ./ requires at all):** 4 files:
  - securityexception.ts — trivial, migrated in spike (0 internal deps)
  - metamodelexception.ts — only external concerto-util
  - dayjs-setup.ts — external only  
  - serializer/validationexception.ts — external only

**Files with only const X = require('./internal') patterns:** ~38 more files
  - These use CJS require syntax, not TypeScript import = require
  - Each migrated file forces any file that requires IT to also migrate
  - The migration is a bottom-up topological traversal of the import graph

**Migration pattern per file:**
  1. Replace: const X = require('./foo')  →  import X from './foo.js'
  2. Replace: const { X, Y } = require('@external')  →  import { X, Y } from '@external'
  3. Replace: export = ClassName  →  export { ClassName }; export default ClassName;
  4. If file uses globalize.ts (Globalize) — must migrate globalize.ts first

**Blocker observed:** Most files depend on concerto-util which is ALSO a bundled CJS-in-ESM blob. This means even after migrating all 58 concerto-core files, tree-shaking INTO concerto-util would still be blocked. Full win requires migrating concerto-util too (estimated ~40 files in packages/concerto-util/src).

**Estimated effort for concerto-core alone:** 58 files, topological order. Most files are mechanical find-replace. Complex files: basemodelmanager.ts (20 internal requires), serializer/jsonpopulator.ts (8+4 requires), factory.ts (10 internal requires). Estimate: 2-3 developer-days for an engineer familiar with the codebase, including test verification.

**tsc TS1203 status:** Not hit during spike because esbuild was used (not tsc) for the after measurement. A tsc-based unbundled ESM build would require tsconfig with module: ESNext or ES2020, which IS supported by tsc — the TS1203 error only fires when you use export = WITH a module: es* setting. Removing export = (replacing with export {}) fully resolves TS1203.

---

### Build Path for Unbundled ESM

Replace the current build:esm step (esbuild bundle:true → single index.mjs blob) with:
  - tsc --module ES2020 --moduleResolution bundler --outDir dist/esm (unbundled, one .mjs per .ts file)
  - OR esbuild with bundle:false and splitting:true
  - package.json exports map to individual files OR a thin re-export barrel

The build:esm script (scripts/build-esm.js) would be simplified — no bundling needed for the ESM path.

---

### VERDICT: GO (conditional on concerto-util co-migration)

**GO** — the per-export tree-shaking benefit is massive and real: 96.2% bundle reduction for a leaf import. The migration pattern is mechanical and well-understood.

**Condition:** Full wins require concerto-util to also migrate from its CJS-in-ESM bundle to native ESM. Without that, consumers still pull in all of concerto-util (~60 KB minified) even for leaf imports. With it, a SecurityException import would likely be <2 KB total.

**Recommended epic scope:**
  1. Migrate concerto-util to native ESM (est. 1-2 days)
  2. Migrate concerto-core to native ESM top-down (est. 2-3 days)
  3. Update tsconfig.build.json: module → ES2020, moduleResolution → bundler
  4. Replace build:esm esbuild bundle:true with tsc unbundled pass
  5. Add exports map entries per module for deep imports (optional)
  6. Verify all downstream packages (concerto-analysis, concerto-vocabulary, etc.) still build
close_reason: Spike complete: GO — 96.2% bundle reduction (596KB→23KB) for leaf import; 58-file migration is mechanical, conditional on concerto-util co-migration
